title: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
description: Explain identity verification versus permission checking.
answer: Authentication verifies who a user or client is. Authorization determines what that authenticated principal is allowed to do. For example, validating a JWT can establish identity and claims, while role or permission checks decide whether the principal may access an admin endpoint.

title: Which HTTP methods are considered idempotent?
description: Define idempotency and give common examples.
answer: An operation is idempotent when repeating the same request has the same intended effect as making it once. `GET`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` are defined as idempotent in HTTP semantics; `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` are also idempotent. `POST` is not generally idempotent, though an API can implement idempotency keys.

title: What is the Saga pattern?
description: Explain how a distributed business transaction can span multiple services.
answer: The Saga pattern breaks a distributed transaction into a sequence of local transactions. If a step fails, compensating transactions can semantically undo earlier steps. A saga can be coordinated through orchestration (a central coordinator) or choreography (services react to events). Compensation is business logic, not a guaranteed database rollback.
